healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system with mandatory health insurance for residents. Tourists pay out-of-pocket. Private healthcare is growing and recommended for visitors.
qualityNotes: Private clinics in Tirana offer adequate care. Public hospitals are underfunded with aging equipment. English-speaking doctors available in Tirana. For serious conditions, medical evacuation to Greece or Italy may be necessary.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (farmaci) open Mon-Sat 8am-8pm. 24/7 pharmacies available in Tirana.
pharmacyTips: Green cross marks pharmacies. Many medications are available OTC at very low prices. Antibiotics often dispensed without prescription. Pharmacists may speak limited English.
prescriptionRules: Many medications available OTC including antibiotics. Controlled substances require prescriptions. Foreign prescriptions not formally accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Require documentation. Bring a doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Albania despite widespread cultivation.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English for controlled medications. Keep all medicines in original packaging.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is essential due to limited healthcare infrastructure. Ensure medical evacuation coverage, especially for remote areas and mountain regions.

recommended: Rabies (for adventure travelers or rural areas)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water in Tirana is generally safe but quality varies. Bottled water is recommended, especially outside the capital and in summer. Bottled water is very cheap.
foodSafetyTips: Albanian cuisine is Mediterranean-influenced and generally safe. Grilled meats and fresh salads are common. Eat at busy restaurants. Coastal seafood is fresh but ensure it's from a reputable restaurant.
medicalTourismNote: Albania is emerging as a dental tourism destination with very affordable prices. Medical tourism is in early stages.
metaDescription: Travel health guide for Albania, emergency 127, Cannabis banned, limited public healthcare. Hospital info, pharmacy tips, vaccinations, and travel insurance.

hospitals.name: American Hospital Tirana
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital. International standards. English-speaking doctors.

hospitals.name: Hygeia Hospital Tirana
hospitals.notes: Part of Greek Hygeia Group. Modern private hospital with international standards.

hospitals.name: University Hospital Center Mother Teresa (QSUT)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Largest in Albania. Emergency services 24/7.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available in Tirana at very affordable prices. Growing dental tourism industry.
dentalCare.costRange: €10-30 for consultation; €20-60 for fillings; €20-80 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Tirana has modern private dental clinics. Prices are among the lowest in Europe. Some clinics specifically target dental tourists.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental clinics in Tirana offer emergency appointments. Hospital emergency departments can handle dental trauma.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some English-speaking psychologists in Tirana.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited. English-speaking support mainly available through private clinics in Tirana or international online platforms.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Albania. Newer buildings in Tirana are improving but older areas and smaller cities have significant barriers.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals are somewhat accessible. Public hospitals have limited accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public transport is not wheelchair accessible. Taxis are the most practical option. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles require advance arrangement.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Tirana's new Skanderbeg Square area is relatively accessible. Historic sites, Berat, Gjirokastër, and the Albanian Riviera have significant accessibility challenges. Plan carefully and contact accommodations in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at private clinics in Tirana.
covidStatus.notes: Albania has lifted all COVID restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics can provide receipts and English-language documentation. Public hospitals may only issue documentation in Albanian. Keep all payment records. Cash is often required at public facilities.
